forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Bank Rate to remain at 3.75% through 2026, falling to 3.25% by spring 2028
findings.detail: Monetary Policy Committee held Bank Rate at 3.75% at both Q1 meetings (30 April and 18 June 2026). MUFG treasury advisors forecast rates to remain on hold through 2026, with next reductions beginning H2 2027, reaching 3.25% by spring 2028, contingent on Consumer Price Index inflation peaking around 3.6%.
findings.matters: Interest rate forecast directly affects GMCA's refinancing strategy and future borrowing costs; peer councils rely on this context for their own borrowing decisions and market timing.
findings.figures: Bank Rate held at 3.75%; PWLB rates at 30 June 2026: 1-year 4.77%, 5-year 5.07%, 10-year 5.55%, 25-year 6.17%; forecast Bank Rate 3.5% by end 2027, 3.25% by spring 2028
findings.quote: We forecast the next reduction in Bank Rate to be made in H2 2027, with Bank Rate falling to a low of 3.25% by the start of 2028.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Authority achieved 4.04% average investment yield, outperforming SONIA by 31 basis points, on track for £9.67m budgeted return
findings.detail: With average funds of £473.7m invested across banks, councils, and money market funds, the authority exceeded Sterling Overnight Index Average returns through active treasury management. Budgeted investment return for 2026/27 of £9.67m is currently forecast to be achieved.
findings.matters: Investment income is material cash generator for the authority; outperformance against SONIA demonstrates effective treasury management and supports cash position.
findings.figures: Average investment rate 4.04% versus SONIA 3.73%; outperformance 0.31bps; budgeted return £9.670m; average funds invested £473.7m
findings.quote: The Authority achieved an average rate of 4.04% which outperformed the average backward looking Sterling Overnight Index Average (SONIA) rate by 0.31 bps. The Authority's budgeted investment return for 2026/27 is £9.670m, and we are currently forecast to achieve this.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Gross external debt forecast at £1,574.4m, £182.9m below budget; net borrowing declining
findings.detail: Both gross external debt and net borrowing are declining from budgeted levels. Gross debt forecast at £1,574.4m versus budget of £1,757.3m, and net borrowing at £1,518.4m versus budget of £1,707.3m. Ratio of financing costs to net revenue stream improving to 6.9% from budgeted 7.6%.
findings.matters: Falling debt across the balance sheet improves credit metrics and reduces refinancing volumes, positive signal to lenders on credit trajectory and debt serviceability.
findings.figures: Gross external debt £1,574.381m (budget £1,757.263m); Net borrowing £1,518.381m (budget £1,707.263m); Ratio of financing costs to net revenue stream 6.9% (budget 7.6%)
findings.quote: Gross external debt as at 31 March £1,757.263m £1,574.381m; Net borrowing as at 31 March £1,707.263m £1,518.381m

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Capital Financing Requirement forecast at £2,688.3m, £305.7m below budget
findings.detail: The Capital Financing Requirement is forecast to fall from budgeted £2,994.0m to £2,688.3m, with annual change in CFR £182.3m against budgeted £453.3m, and in-year borrowing requirement £370.0m against budgeted £567.0m. The paper does not explain whether this represents slippage in capital delivery, deferral of planned projects, or efficiency improvements.
findings.matters: A 10% reduction in planned capital investment affects both immediate borrowing need and the multi-year capital programme outlook; peer councils monitoring how others manage capital programmes in the current market, and lenders assessing whether deferral indicates financial constraint or prudent timing.
findings.figures: Capital expenditure £994.747m (budget £1,148.913m); Capital Financing Requirement £2,688.288m (budget £2,994.019m); Annual change in CFR £182.271m (budget £453.281m); In year borrowing requirement £370.000m (budget £566.956m)
findings.quote: Prudential Indicators 2025/26 Budget 2026/27 Forecast Capital expenditure £1,148.913m £994.747m Capital Financing Requirement (CFR) £2,994.019m £2,688.288m

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Opinion GMCA 2025-26 v1.2 Final
findings.headline: £72m of grant funding certified as spent in accordance with grant conditions
findings.detail: All 11 grant certifications in 2025/26 received positive assurance, covering £72.055m, confirming compliant spend on Local Energy Advice Demonstrators, Growth Hub, SHDF, 5G Innovations, Brownfield Housing Fund, Net Zero programmes and Made Smarter grants.
findings.matters: Demonstrates compliance with grant conditions, which protects the council from grant clawback or restrictions on future funding.
findings.figures: £72.055m total across 11 grants; all positive assurance
findings.quote: All grant certification work in 2025/26 received positive assurance, confirming that £72m of grant funding was spent in accordance with the relevant grant conditions.
